title: Self-Healing Action Verification against Instruction Tampering and Sensor Failures in Humanoid Robots
abstract: As humanoid robots are increasingly used in complex real-world environments, reliable verification of robot actions becomes more important. Action verification should not only check whether the executed action matches the intended instruction, but also keep reliable performance when motor-sensor observations are affected by failures. Traditional instruction authentication mainly protects the instruction itself and cannot directly verify the final physical action of the robot. In addition, the sensing information used to observe robot execution may also become unreliable. In this paper, we propose a self-healing motor-based action verification framework that combines explainable sensor selection, temporal masked reconstruction, and multiscale action recognition. First, Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) are used to identify motor encoders that provide important information for action discrimination. Then, the selected encoder signals are processed by a temporal masked reconstruction model to recover unreliable joint observations based on temporal continuity and cross-joint coordination. After that, a multiscale gallery recognizer with zero trainable classifier parameters is used to infer the physical action executed by the robot. The inferred action is finally compared with the trusted intended instruction to detect instruction-execution inconsistency. The proposed framework is evaluated on a Booster Robotics K1 Education humanoid robot under multiple sensor-failure modes and different corruption levels, and is compared with several existing methods. The proposed method achieves average accuracies of 98.4% and 94.8% for single-action and compound-action recognition, respectively. Under different sensor-failure levels, the proposed self-healing method achieves an average recognition accuracy of 92.6%.

title: VLCQ: Post-training quantization for deep neural networks using variable length coding
abstract: Quantization plays a crucial role in efficiently deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Post-training quantization does not require access to the original dataset or retraining the full model. Current methods that achieve high performance close to baseline results typically require INT8 fixed-point integers. However, achieving higher model compression with lower bit-widths often leads to significant performance degradation. In this paper, we propose VLCQ, a post-training quantization method that relaxes the fixed-point encoding constraint, enabling more flexible exploration of quantization techniques through variable-length encoding. This approach achieves competitive or improved performance while reducing bit-widths, without requiring access to training data or model fine-tuning. Extensive experiments on image classification, segmentation, and object detection demonstrate that VLCQ improves model compression and accuracy compared with state-of-the-art post-training quantization approaches. For per-channel quantization, VLCQ surpasses FP32 accuracy and Piece-Wise Linear Quantization (PWLQ) on most evaluated models, achieving up to 6x compression compared with FP32 and up to 1.7x compared with PWLQ. When prioritizing compression with limited accuracy loss, VLCQ achieves up to 12.25x compression compared with FP32 with less than 4% performance degradation. For per-tensor quantization, VLCQ is competitive with Data-Free Quantization (DFQ), while providing greater flexibility to achieve lower bit rates across different tasks and models.

title: Fine-Tuning Strategy, Not Just Data: A Statistically Rigorous Audit of Gender and Stereotypical Bias in Embedding Models for HR Recommendation Systems
abstract: Embedding models underpin modern job-candidate matching: resumes, job descriptions, and queries are encoded as dense vectors, and recommendations come from nearest-neighbor retrieval over that space. Any social bias in the embeddings therefore feeds directly into HR recommendations. We audit six multilingual sentence-embedding models (LaBSE- and E5-family, both public and custom fine-tuned) using Bias-in-Bios (occupational gender bias) and StereoSet (stereotypes across profession, race, gender, and religion). We treat statistical validity as a first-class concern: we identify a non-independence error in a naive significance test, where pooling non-independent pairwise similarities inflated a trivial 0.0046 mean difference to $p \approx 0$, and replace it with a profession-level paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, individual-resampling bootstrap confidence intervals, and permutation tests for StereoSet. Under the corrected methodology, knowledge-distillation (KD) fine-tuning of E5-Base significantly increases measured bias on Bias-in-Bios ($Δ= -0.177$, $p < 10^{-8}$; more negative means more bias), although this measure is sensitive to global embedding geometry. The KD result is corroborated by pro-stereotype patterns in the StereoSet profession category (uncorrected $p < 0.05$). Binary-classification fine-tuning of the same base model shows no statistically distinguishable change ($p = 0.218$). Fine-tuning strategy is thus an actionable design lever for practitioners building HR recommenders. We also report which benchmark categories are underpowered, and note that two domain-adapted models could not be included in significance testing due to a software-access constraint, which limits our conclusions.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Science and Technology: A Critical Narrative Review of Applications, Evidence, Risks and Emerging Directions
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a general-purpose set of computational methods that is increasingly embedded in scientific research and technological systems. This critical narrative review evaluates the principal roles of AI across scientific discovery, medicine, environmental and space science, manufacturing, software engineering, cybersecurity and communication networks, while distinguishing demonstrated capabilities from claims that remain context dependent. The review also examines conceptual differences between task-bounded AI and human intelligence, and considers human–AI collaboration as a practical design problem rather than a contest between interchangeable forms of intelligence. Literature was selected through transparent live scholarly searching and verification, with an emphasis on peer-reviewed evidence, primary studies for prominent performance claims and authoritative governance sources. The evidence indicates that AI is especially useful where large, high-dimensional or multimodal data must be classified, modelled or searched, and where repeated decisions can be evaluated against explicit performance criteria. Examples include protein-structure prediction, anomaly detection, remote-sensing analysis, autonomous planetary navigation, smart manufacturing and cyber-threat analysis. Nevertheless, high benchmark performance does not automatically establish clinical utility, causal understanding, robustness under distribution shift, safety or equitable deployment. Major cross-cutting limitations include data quality, representativeness, opaque decision processes, evaluation leakage, infrastructure requirements, environmental cost, cybersecurity vulnerabilities and uneven institutional capacity. Responsible integration therefore requires task-specific validation, human oversight, traceability, monitoring and governance proportional to potential harm. Future progress will depend less on simply increasing model scale than on improving scientific validity, causal and mechanistic integration, reproducibility, context-sensitive evaluation and access in lower-resource settings. AI is best understood as an enabling technology whose scientific and social value depends on the quality of the evidence, institutions and human judgement surrounding its use.

title: O‘ZBEK TILI UCHUN TASVIR-TIL MODELLARINI ADAPTIV MOSLASHTIRISHNI MATEMATIK MODELLASHTIRISH
abstract: Tasvir va o‘zbekcha matn o‘rtasidagi semantik moslikni aniqlash masalasi parametrik optimallashtirish shaklida qaraladi. Ishda tasvir-matn juftligi sifati, namuna murakkabligi va yozuv variantlarining mosligini hisobga oluvchi matematik model taklif etiladi. Maqsad funksiyasi kontrastiv yo‘qotish, yozuvlararo muvofiqlik va regulyarizatsiya hadlaridan tuziladi. Parametrlarni hisoblash uchun mini-paketli gradient usuli, adaptiv vaznlash va past rangli parametrizatsiya birlashtiriladi. Taklifning samaradorligini tekshirishga mo‘ljallangan hisoblash tajribasi mezonlari belgilanadi.

title: BLOKLI SIMMETRIK SHIFRLASH ALGORITMLARINI KRIPTOTAHLIL QILISH MASALALARI
abstract: Ushbu maqolada blokli simmetrik shifrlash algoritmlarining kriptobardoshliligini baholashning zamonaviy usullari va ularning kriptotahlili tahlil qilingan. Kriptoanalitik ixtiyoridagi ma'lumotlar hajmi va turiga qarab shifrmatn, aniqlangan ochiq matn, tanlangan ochiq matn, tanlangan shifrmatn va tanlangan matn asosidagi hujumlarning o'ziga xos xususiyatlari tavsiflangan. Shuningdek, to'liq tanlov, statistik, chiziqli, differensial, chiziqli-differensial, slaydli, integral va algebraik kriptotahlil usullarining nazariy asoslari ko'rib chiqilgan. Chiziqli va differensial kriptotahlil usullarining matematik mohiyati, ularni blokli shifrlash algoritmlarida qo'llash imkoniyatlari hamda kalitni aniqlash jarayonidagi ahamiyati tahlil qilingan. Kriptografik algoritmning himoyalanganlik darajasini aniqlashda kalitlar fazosining hajmi, hisoblash murakkabligi, zarur bo'lgan ochiq va shifrmatnlar soni hamda kriptotahlil uchun sarflanadigan hisoblash resurslari muhim mezonlar sifatida baholandi. title: Deterministic Supremacy: Solving Quantum Computing Challenges (QHACK) via the IPM Model
abstract: This document aims to demonstrate the epistemological and computational superiority of the IPM (Information Projection Model) over contemporary quantum computing platforms. The IPM establishes that the three-dimensional reality we experience is, in fact, a discrete geometric projection of information, encoded onto a discrete two-dimensional topological root.

title: Sequence-Structured Decision Learning for Branch-and-Bound in Mixed-Integer Linear Programming
abstract: Branch-and-bound (BnB) solves mixed-integer linear programs by constructing and exploring a search tree. Node selection and branching are two recurrent decisions that directly determine the tree. Learning-based approaches typically optimize either decision in isolation and condition on a mostly local view, leaving the coupled evolution of the search tree insufficiently modeled. This paper proposes Seq-BnB, a sequence-structured framework that learns branching and node selection from a shared global representation of the evolving BnB process. Seq-BnB serializes node creations, node updates, node-selection events, and branching events into typed tokens, producing a causal event sequence of the search trajectory. A self-attention encoder summarizes this global search history, a bipartite graph neural network encodes the current LP relaxation, and context-conditioned decision heads score branching variables and open nodes. To reduce distribution shift between expert demonstrations and learned policies, Seq-BnB is trained with DAgger-style data aggregation. On four MILP benchmark families, Seq-BnB consistently processes fewer BnB nodes than heuristic and learning-based baselines, with strong solution times on both standard and larger transfer instances. While this paper evaluates Seq-BnB instantiation for branching and node selection, it accommodates additional solver decisions, such as cut selection, by introducing new action tokens and decision heads.

title: OʻZBEK TILI MATNLARIDA SEMANTIK MUNOSABATLARNI ANIQLASHNING GIBRID MATEMATIK MODELI VA ALGORITMI
abstract: Oʻzbek tili matnlarida soʻz tartibi, affiksal shakllar va kontekst almashinuvi tokenlar oʻrtasidagi semantik aloqalarni yagona qoidalar asosida aniqlashni qiyinlashtiradi. Mavjud yondashuvlarda aksiomatik belgilar bilan vektorli oʻxshashlikni birlashtirish va qaror chegarasining barqarorligini formal asoslash masalasi yetarlicha aniqlashtirilmagan. Taklif etilgan gibrid model aksiomatik-deduktiv usul, teorema-isbot tuzilmasi va iteratsion hisoblashga tayangan holda har bir token juftligiga belgi hamda vektorli baho biriktiradi. Maksimal baho yagona boʻlganda semantik sinf bir qiymatli tanlanadi. Nazariy tahlilda algoritmning vaqt murakkabligi O(n) ekani, qaror chegarasidagi maksimal xatolik 1,2 foizdan oshmasligi va iteratsion jarayonning barqarorligi isbotlandi. Natijalar gibrid baholashning qoidaviy va sonli komponentlarini yagona matematik mezonga keltirishini koʻrsatadi. Modelni keyingi bosqichda nazoratlanmagan klasterlashtirish, PCA va oʻz-diqqat mexanizmi asosidagi vektorli tasvirlash bilan kengaytirish tavsiya etiladi.

title: La titularidad de los derechos de autor de las obras musicales generadas por inteligencia artificial: desafíos jurídicos para Ecuador
abstract: El artículo analizó a quién corresponde la titularidad de los derechos de autor sobre las obras musicales generadas mediante inteligencia artificial y qué desafíos plantea su regulación en Ecuador. Un estudio cualitativo, doctrinal y comparado examinó la Decisión 351 de la Comunidad Andina, el Código Orgánico de la Economía Social de los Conocimientos, Creatividad e Innovación, la legislación británica sobre obras generadas por computadora, la Directiva (UE) 2019/790, la práctica de la Oficina de Derechos de Autor de los Estados Unidos y doctrina arbitrada. Se constató que el ordenamiento andino y ecuatoriano exige una autoría humana, por lo que la música generada de forma autónoma carece de autor protegido, mientras que las obras con aportación creativa humana determinante sí pueden protegerse. Se identificaron como desafíos el grado de intervención humana exigible, el uso de obras protegidas para entrenar los sistemas y la transparencia. Se proponen criterios para una reforma prudente.

title: A Linkable Anonymous and Verifiable Sealed-Bid Auction Scheme for Consortium Blockchain
abstract: Sealed-bid auctions require bidders to submit concealed bids within a prescribed bidding period, after which the bids are opened and compared to determine the highest bidder. However, existing auction systems still face challenges in protecting bidder privacy and bid data, verifying auction results, and reducing dependence on centralized auctioneers. This paper proposes LAV-Auction, a linkable anonymous and verifiable sealed-bid auction scheme for consortium blockchain. A registration authority publishes a ring of eligible public keys. Each bidder submits a commitment, a bid ciphertext containing the bid value and commitment randomness, and an auction-scoped linkable ring signature. The signature hides which registered key was used, while its key image enables the contract to reject repeated bids from the same credential in the same auction. After the contract fixes the accepted record order, the auction committee decrypts the bid ciphertexts. A verifier recomputes the digest of the frozen ledger records. It then verifies a Groth16 proof showing that the announced winner corresponds to a valid frozen bid with the highest value. LAV-Auction provides bidder anonymity, bid confidentiality before committee decryption, duplicate bid prevention, and verifiable winner correctness over the frozen valid bid set. Experiments on a Hyperledger Fabric implementation demonstrate practical computation, communication, and scalability trade-offs. The results show that LAV-Auction achieves millisecond-level result verification through succinct Groth16 proofs while maintaining compact result certification payloads under increasing bidder scales.

title: Self-Evolving Visual Agent via Margin Reward
abstract: Visual agents that interleave reasoning with tool invocation have posed a promising direction for multimodal tasks. However, learning effective tool invocation usually relies on curated question-answer pairs or expert demonstrations at scale, which are expensive to acquire. In this study, we propose Marvo, a simple-yet-effective self-evolution approach that enables learning tool invocation from unlabeled images. Marvo consists of two agents: (1) a challenger that generates question-answer pairs from unlabeled images, and (2) a solver that learns tool invocation by solving questions through reinforcement learning. To encourage effective tool invocation, a good training question should be difficult enough to warrant tool use, yet remain within the solver's capabilities. To this end, we introduce a margin reward to the challenger, defined as solver's performance difference with and without access to tools. With the margin reward, we create an adaptive curriculum that encourages the solver to learn effective tool invocation. Across benchmarks covering agentic reasoning, visual search, mathematical, and general real-world reasoning, Marvo improves average accuracy by up to 7.1\% --- demonstrating margin reward as a preferred way to scale question complexity without human supervision.

title: From Video to Vision: Learning Generalizable Humanoid Carrying from Human Motion
abstract: Most existing approaches rely on video or motion-capture data for reinforcement learning (RL) training; however, all of these methods require an upper-level module to generate reference trajectories in real time. In object carrying tasks, the humanoid can only lift objects from designated locations along the reference trajectory, resulting in poor spatial generalization. Moreover, existing policies can only be evaluated inside a motion-capture studio. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MOVER}, a multi-stage, Teacher-Assistant-Student, RL training framework for humanoid object carrying. We first collect data from videos and employ GENMO and GMR to retarget the video data, combining this with data augmentation techniques to generalize the data across objects of varying shapes and sizes. In the \textbf{first stage}, building upon the DeepMimic \cite{peng2018deepmimic} motion-training framework, we train the humanoid to transport objects from specified locations along designated trajectories. In the \textbf{second stage}, we relax the tracking of the reference motion and adjust the reward so that the humanoid learns to transport objects from different positions. In the \textbf{third stage}, we apply a Dagger-PPO distillation method to distill away the proprioceptive position observations and reference joint position of the humanoid. This allows the deployed policy to operate without relying on global position information from a motion-capture system; instead, the humanoid can directly perceive the object's pose from its onboard RGB-D camera to complete the carrying task. We design a series of simulation experiments to compare the success rates across stages (Stages 1 vs. 2) and before versus after distillation. We further transfer the policy to a real humanoid, successfully transporting objects at varying positions in a motion-capture-free setting.

title: Minimax Wasserstein Testing under Differential Privacy
abstract: We study Wasserstein-$p$ goodness-of-fit and two-sample testing under differential privacy. For general compact metric spaces, we establish upper and lower bounds on the minimax separation radii in terms of covering numbers, matching up to logarithmic factors. On the hypercube $[0,1]^d$, these bounds match up to constant factors for two-sample testing in all dimensions and for goodness-of-fit testing whenever $d\neq 4p$, thereby closing logarithmic gaps in existing non-private results. At the critical case $(d,p)=(4,1)$, we further show that a logarithmic factor is unavoidable by establishing matching minimax bounds for non-private Wasserstein-$1$ goodness-of-fit testing under a bounded-density assumption. Finally, for unbounded domains, we establish minimax-optimal separation rates up to logarithmic factors under an exponential tail condition.

title: KPGrasp: Scalable Keypoint Flow Matching for Dexterous Grasp Generation
abstract: Generating high-quality dexterous grasps remains challenging for learning-based methods, which often depend on carefully tuned contact losses or costly contact-based test-time refinement. We present KPGrasp, a flow-matching framework that learns dexterous grasp priors from large-scale data rather than relying on contact losses or contact-based test-time refinement. KPGrasp couples an all-Euclidean 3D hand-keypoint parameterization with a simple yet scalable Transformer flow model. The parameterization avoids the drawbacks of the conventional mixed SE(3) pose and joint-angle output space, expresses grasps in the same frame as the object point cloud, and thus enables native spatial reasoning; the Transformer flow model is trained with only the standard flow-matching loss and scales effectively with data, model capacity, and batch size. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on two simulation benchmarks. On the Dexonomy benchmark, it reaches a 76.3% grasp success rate, improving over the strongest directly comparable baseline by 47.4% while reducing penetration depth to 2.4 mm. The same model also achieves the best average performance on the DexGrasp Anything benchmark without fine-tuning. For batched inference, KPGrasp requires only 0.032 s per grasp. Finally, real-world experiments on 20 diverse objects demonstrate that the pipeline can be deployed in a real-world setup. Project Page: https://yuansen-huang.github.io/KPGrasp-page/

title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
abstract: Abstract In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

title: The Role of AI-Powered Search in Shaping Consumer Search Behaviour: An Empirical Study among Students in Private Universities in AP.
abstract: This study examines the role of AI-powered search in shaping consumer search behaviour among students in private universities in Andhra Pradesh. AI-powered search tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and Perplexity are changing how users find, evaluate, compare, and use information. The study focuses on students’ awareness and usage of AI-powered search, its influence on information-search habits, perceptions of usefulness, convenience and relevance, trust and verification of AI-generated information, and its effect on product and service comparison and purchase-related decision-making. A quantitative, descriptive, cross-sectional research design was used. The empirical analysis was conducted using 84 valid questionnaire responses collected via Google Forms. The collected data were analysed using frequency and percentage analysis, mean and standard deviation, Cronbach’s Alpha, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The study provides insights into changing consumer information-search patterns in the AI era and offers useful implications for digital marketers seeking to adapt content, search visibility, and consumer-engagement strategies to AI-mediated search environments.

title: An Empirical Study on AI-Driven Consumer Insights
abstract: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming the way businesses understand consumers, analyse behavioural patterns, and make marketing and business decisions. The present study, “An Empirical Study on AI-Driven Consumer Insights,” examines the role of AI in generating consumer insights, analysing consumer behaviour, influencing purchasing decisions, improving personalised marketing, and supporting business decision-making. The study also considers the importance of ethical AI practices, privacy, transparency, trust, and responsible use of consumer data. Primary data were collected from 128 respondents from Mumbai, and the data were analysed using tabulation and the Chi-Square test. The findings indicate statistically significant responses across all six hypotheses. The results suggest that respondents perceive AI as an important tool for generating consumer insights, improving consumer behaviour analysis, influencing purchasing decisions, enhancing personalised marketing, and supporting business decisions. The findings also highlight the importance of ethical AI practices in consumer data collection. The study concludes that AI-driven consumer insights can provide significant value to businesses when implemented effectively, transparently, and responsibly. evidence.title: An Empirical Study on AI-Driven Consumer Insights
evidence.abstract: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming the way businesses understand consumers, analyse behavioural patterns, and make marketing and business decisions. The present study, “An Empirical Study on AI-Driven Consumer Insights,” examines the role of AI in generating consumer insights, analysing consumer behaviour, influencing purchasing decisions, improving personalised marketing, and supporting business decision-making. The study also considers the importance of ethical AI practices, privacy, transparency, trust, and responsible use of consumer data. Primary data were collected from 128 respondents from Mumbai, and the data were analysed using tabulation and the Chi-Square test. The findings indicate statistically significant responses across all six hypotheses. The results suggest that respondents perceive AI as an important tool for generating consumer insights, improving consumer behaviour analysis, influencing purchasing decisions, enhancing personalised marketing, and supporting business decisions. The findings also highlight the importance of ethical AI practices in consumer data collection. The study concludes that AI-driven consumer insights can provide significant value to businesses when implemented effectively, transparently, and responsibly. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Consumer Insights, Consumer Behaviour, Personalised Marketing, Purchasing Behaviour, Business Decision-Making, Ethical AI.

title: FLE: Fast Local Experts — an 89 GB Mixture-of-Experts model at ~90 tokens/s on one 32 GB GPU
abstract: We run Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 512-expert Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model, on a single workstation with one 32 GB GPU, 120 GB of system RAM and 16 CPU cores. Two pieces make this practical. First, FLE-IQ3_M (internally G3), a hybrid quantization that combines the Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS release with expert layers from ISTA-DASLab's GSQ-RCO release: 88.87 GB instead of 93.68 GB, with a KL divergence against BF16 that stays within the measurement noise on three texts, one of them held out. Second, FLE, a fork of llama.cpp that borrows ideas and some code from ik_llama.cpp, FreeToken, KTransformers and Strata (Section 8): a GPU expert cache with frequency-gated admission and oldest-first eviction, overlap of GPU cache hits with CPU work on cache misses, fused CUDA kernels, and speculative decoding with the model's own multi-token-prediction (MTP) head, its experts requantized to IQ4_NL. Against current upstream llama.cpp (commit a8c9a4e7c, newer than FLE's base), with the same FLE-IQ3_M file, the same card and the same 16 threads (no expert cache, no MTP), the final FLE configuration decodes 2.49 times as fast as upstream with micro-batch 1024 (−59.9 % [95 % CI −61.2 .. −58.5] for upstream in a paired bracket, B1e) and 2.78 times as fast as upstream with micro-batch 4096 (−64.0 % [−65.2 .. −62.9]); FLE runs at about 100 tokens/s on these prompts. Prefill is where FLE still loses: upstream with micro-batch 4096 processes 4k and 8.6k prompts 24 % and 12 % faster, and Strata, the closest public engine, 2.3 to 2.7 times as fast, while FLE decodes 23 % faster than Strata. Against our own previous production setup (stock build with Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, ~56 tokens/s) FLE was +58.5 % faster [+55.8 .. +61.6] already before the last steps (bracket END2). On three benchmarks from Qwen's model card, one run each, FLE-IQ3_M on FLE is level with the card on IFBench (80.3 strict / 83.0 loose against 81.3) and GPQA Diamond (88.9 against 91.7, inside the 95 % interval) and below it on LiveCodeBench v6 (85.5 against 91.9, outside the interval; 10 of the 19 failures are answers cut off at the 81,920-token limit). Besides FLE-IQ3_M we release two smaller hybrids and FLE-IQ3_M-REAP448, with 64 of 512 experts per layer pruned by REAP; a 400-question MKQA knowledge probe shows that KLD on a few texts understates what pruning removes (at 384 experts per layer the KLD rose moderately, while correct answers fell by 5.8 / 11.8 points in German / English). We report the negative results as well: expert prefetching by pre-gating, n-gram drafting, low-rank kernels and fully self-made quantizations all lost in our measurements, and so did copying part of the cache misses over PCIe as Strata does (−4.5 %) and a rebase of the fork onto current upstream (−5.7 %). A re-trained MTP head (recursive self-distillation) gained +4.54 % only on the tasks its training corpus contained; on 16 unseen tasks the untrained head was +2.95 % [+1.96 .. +3.93] faster than it, so the release ships the untrained head. The speed numbers above were measured with the re-trained head c2 (Section 4.3). This archive holds release v1.0.1 of the FLE engine together with the technical report (docs/fle/fle-paper-v1.0.1.pdf). FLE is a fork of llama.cpp (MIT, copyright the ggml authors); it takes code from ik_llama.cpp and Strata and re-implements parts of FreeToken (see the NOTICE files). The engine code is identical to v1.0 (commit b3f2544ca); v1.0.1 adds the report and links. Report with films (HTML): https://sirfyyn.github.io/FastLocalExperts/Model files (GGUF): https://huggingface.co/sirfyyn/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FLE-GGUFFilms "Making Rhea Fast": https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMYhpsBSEhIQ

title: Measuring Self-Checking Without Reader Bias: Data and Results (Anonymous Review Artifact)
abstract: Review artifact for a paper on measuring what a language model's check of its own answer does. It holds the side-blind answer key (the final answer each response settles on and whether it is right), the human labels, the final result files behind each table and figure, and the analysis scripts. Model responses, raw judge replies, the trained reader weights and the training code are withheld during review and will be released on acceptance. See README.md for the map from paper items to files.

title: GAMW: Generation-Aware Mel-Domain Watermarking for TTS Traceability
abstract: As text-to-speech (TTS) systems continue to advance, provenance tracking and security verification of synthesized speech have become increasingly important. Audio watermarking provides active provenance by embedding imperceptible, machine-recoverable information into speech. However, existing post-hoc methods typically modify the waveform after synthesis, leaving the watermark vulnerable to compound perturbations. To address this limitation, we propose GAMW, a watermark injection framework integrated into the TTS generation process. Before waveform synthesis, GAMW embeds a content-adaptive multi-bit watermark residual into the generated representation, and its decoding objective combines focal modulation with dynamic per-bit weighting. We train and evaluate GAMW separately on two TTS backbones. With a 16-bit payload, GAMW improves decoding accuracy over the strongest baseline by 9.2 and 23.5 percentage points under individual and compound perturbations, respectively, while maintaining competitive speech quality. Reliable clean-speech decoding is also retained at higher payloads. Code is available at https://github.com/ZConJugaTe/GAMW.

title: NOANIQ VA KATTA HAJMLI AXBOROT OQIMLARINI INTELLEKTUAL QAYTA ISHLASH UCHUN MODIFIKATSIYALANGAN NEYRO-TARMOQLI ALGORITMLARNI ISHLAB CHIQISH
abstract: Mazkur maqolada noaniq, shovqinli va katta hajmli axborot oqimlarini intellektual qayta ishlash uchun modifikatsiyalangan neyro-tarmoqli algoritmlarni ishlab chiqish masalalari tahlil qilinadi. Katta ma’lumotlar oqimining o‘zgaruvchanligi, yetishmayotgan qiymatlar, anomal kuzatuvlar va ma’lumotlar taqsimotining vaqt davomida o‘zgarishi kabi muammolar ko‘rib chiqiladi. Neyro-tarmoq arxitekturalarini adaptiv o‘qitish, diqqat mexanizmlari, anomal holatlarni aniqlash, noaniqlikni baholash va modelni hisoblash jihatdan optimallashtirish imkoniyatlari asoslab beriladi. Shuningdek, vaqt oynalari asosida ma’lumotlarni qayta ishlash, inkremental o‘qitish va model parametrlarini dinamik yangilashning samaradorligi yoritiladi. Taklif etilayotgan yondashuvning telekommunikatsiya, sanoat, qishloq xo‘jaligi, energetika, axborot xavfsizligi va boshqa sohalarda qo‘llash imkoniyatlari ko‘rsatib beriladi. Tadqiqot natijalari katta hajmli axborot oqimlaridan muhim bilimlarni tezkor ajratib olish, prognozlash aniqligini oshirish va qaror qabul qilish jarayonining ishonchliligini ta’minlash uchun ilmiy asos yaratadi.

title: Projection tests fail for three centred Gaussian components
abstract: Unrefereed analytic counterexample: one centred planar Gaussian is below a mixture of three centred Gaussians in every projected convex order but not in multivariate convex order. Exact rational covariances and a six-affine-function witness give a strict expectation gap. A specified common-noise perturbation makes every covariance positive definite. Internal exact checks and uncertified quadrature corroborate the written proof; no formal verification, external peer review or absolute priority is claimed. Comparison with Jourdain–Pagès is to arXiv v1, not the unavailable final journal body.

title: A Closed-Form Excess-Population Latency Budget for Active Reset of Superconducting Qubits
abstract: Active reset returns a superconducting qubit to its ground state: read it out, apply a π-pulse if it reads excited. The classical decision between the two takes time, and the qubit relaxes meanwhile. Salathé and co-workers tied this cost to the ratio of feedback latency to lifetime and expected the error to scale as one minus its exponential, and Ristè and co-workers had already written the reset error to first order as readout errors plus equilibration terms linear in the latency. This work makes that accounting exact at a fixed evaluation time. A transmon with T₁ = 50 μs is prepared in its excited state and read out by an ideal terminal projection followed by a classical confusion channel with symmetric assignment error P_AE. Under that instrument the ensemble-averaged residual population after one feedback cycle is an exact weighted sum of four deterministic Lindblad evolutions, conditioned on the projected and the reported outcome. The sum is evaluated in closed form, together with the critical latency τ_crit at which the residual exceeds its zero-latency value by a chosen budget, defined throughout as an absolute increase in excitation probability of 0.01, that is one percentage point. To leading order τ_crit is the budget times T₁ divided by the pulse-firing probability p_pulse, times a prefactor of 1.019 for the parameters considered here. Discarding that prefactor while retaining the division by p_pulse costs under 2%; the further simplification to budget times T₁ carries 3.4% to 7.3% error across P_AE = 1% to 5%. Because P_AE enters only through p_pulse, the budget is weakly sensitive to assignment error over the tested range for an initially excited qubit, giving 518 to 539 ns; the readout duration enters separately, through the observation window and the post-readout population. A critical latency exists only for budgets below the maximum excess attainable within that window. The four-branch representation is exact for the stated measurement model; the finite-pulse map used to evaluate it is approximate, and is replaced here by its exact affine propagator. The closed form agrees with a master-equation solver to 3.3×10⁻⁷ and is cross-checked against stochastic trajectories.

title: Pegi1727/DIINA-ASR-Dynamic-Inhibition-Induced-Neural-Architecture-for-Under-Resourced-Languages: DIINA: Dynamic Inhibition-Induced Neural Architecture – A Comparative ASR Analysis of Scottish Gaelic and South Azerbaijani (ICPLA 2027)
abstract: Abstract: This repository provides the empirical data, source code, and computational models associated with the research manuscript: "Mitigating Computational Recognition Errors in Under-Resourced Speech: A Mixed-Effects Evaluation of Contact-Induced ASR Drift in Scottish Gaelic and South Azerbaijani," presented at ICPLA 2027. Research Context: The DIINA (Dynamic Inhibition-Induced Neural Architecture) framework is a cognitive-inspired ASR mitigation strategy developed to counter "cross-lingual leakage" and "morpho-phonemic cannibalization." The research compares the effectiveness of DIINA against standard ASR baselines in two under-resourced speech varieties: Scottish Gaelic (Gàidhlig) and South Azerbaijani. Repository Contents: Statistical Pipeline: R-based mixed-effects modeling scripts (mixed_effects_lme4.R) and diagnostic coefficient tables quantifying WER variance across speech regimes (Archival, Media, Spontaneous). Computational Architecture: Core implementation of the DIINA inhibitory gates (Python), showcasing the evolution from static logit-level gating to integrated Latent Representation Control. Experimental Data: Standardized audio dataset manifests (EBU R128 compliant) and high-fidelity transcription annotation protocols. Visual Artifacts: Publication-ready visual documentation, including the project's Graphical Abstract and taxonomy heatmaps. Findings: The study demonstrates a significant lexical-level inhibition success in Scottish Gaelic (+4.54% WER improvement), while documenting the structural limits of post-decoding filters in the South Azerbaijani manifold, where structural drift necessitates deeper architectural interventions. Keywords: Computational Cognition ASR Scottish Gaelic South Azerbaijani Mixed-effects Modeling DIINA Under-resourced Languages ICPLA 2027 Speech Technology

title: Entanglement-assisted coherent control for deterministic quantum gate teleportation
abstract: Abstract Quantum gate teleportation enables spatially separated parties to implement nonlocal quantum operations using preshared entanglement, local operations, measurement, and classical communication. Here, we present a two-branch entanglement-assisted coherent-control architecture for the deterministic remote implementation of nonlocal two-qubit gates. In this architecture, the two parties coherently select between two pairs of local unitary operations acting on their respective input qubits, a structure that can be naturally encoded through spatial-path superposition. The protocol is formulated at the operator level, allowing deterministic operation to be established independently of the input-state parametrization and making its scope explicit. For two-qubit unitary targets, we show that the deterministic branch conditions restrict the nonlocal domain of the balanced two-branch ansatz: apart from local product operations, any implementable nonlocal unitary must be locally unitarily equivalent to the CNOT/CZ class. We construct explicit CNOT and controlled- Z realizations as two representatives of this unique nonlocal equivalence class. We also introduce a photonic path-encoding and destructive branch-readout scheme in which spatial path encodes the coherent-control degree of freedom and polarization carries the computational qubits, illustrating how the proposed architecture can be physically encoded.

For two-qubit unitary targets, we show that the deterministic branch conditions restrict the nonlocal domain of the balanced two-branch ansatz: apart from local product operations, any implementable nonlocal unitary must be locally unitarily equivalent to the CNOT/CZ class. We construct explicit CNOT and controlled- Z realizations as two representatives of this unique nonlocal equivalence class. We also introduce a photonic path-encoding and destructive branch-readout scheme in which spatial path encodes the coherent-control degree of freedom and polarization carries the computational qubits, illustrating how the proposed architecture can be physically encoded.

title: Evaluation of physical training effectiveness for college students based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: The physical training of college students can be made more productive with the help of adaptive approaches. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) offers training policies that are more customized based on performance and physiological measurements and are superior to fixed schedules. The first goal is to make a smart system that will be efficient in physical training optimization with the help of DRL. Research suggests the Hare Escape-Search Functional Dueling Deep Q-Network (HE-FDDQN), which is a DRL algorithm that predicts student states, actions, and rewards in order to maximize training policies. Dueling architecture improves state-value learning, while escape-search enhances exploration for adaptive offline training recommendations. The College Student Physical Training Dataset was used for evaluation, which is a public data set consisting of 1000 records from the measurements of the wearable devices, fitness tests, and self-reported physical activity indicators. Preprocessing includes data cleaning, synchronization of data, and normalization of data. Python implementations exhibit effective policy learning, and visualization reveals that the development of fitness and less overtraining is possible. The HE-FDDQN model demonstrated great regression ability (MAE 1.17, RMSE 1.52, R 2 0.931), and good classification scores, recall 0.922, precision 0.913, accuracy 0.925, AUC 0.912, and F1-score 0.909. The Dueling DQN strategy achieved better rewards and convergence, supporting adaptive recommendations under offline experimental evaluation. Overall, the results suggest that HE-FDDQN can enhance the assessment and personalization of college students' physical training, offering an efficient and customized alternative to fixed training plans with the potential to improve fitness outcomes.

title: Optimize Once, Execute Fast: Latency-Aware Multi-Agent Workflow Learning for Recurrent Queries
abstract: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-based MAS) have shown remarkable success in solving complex tasks by coordinating specialized agents through multi-step workflows. To overcome the high cost and specificity of manually designed workflows, recent research has shifted toward learning them automatically. However, a key limitation remains: while agent calls introduce significant latency due to model inference time and service congestion, most automated methods optimize solely for downstream performance, ignoring execution time (makespan). This issue is amplified when workflows are reused across recurring queries, making latency accumulate over time. This limits deployment in recurrent applications such as AI customer support and AI cloud troubleshooting, where users expect fast responses. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new problem, termed latency-aware workflow generation, where the objective is to minimize workflow makespan while aiming to retain downstream performance. We propose LAWA (Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion), a novel framework that reduces makespan via theoretically grounded graph edits targeting critical-path bottlenecks. By unifying a graph generator with this graph-editing procedure, LAWA supports both de novo workflow generation and refinement of existing ones. Empirical results across seven benchmarks demonstrate that LAWA significantly reduces makespan while achieving competitive task performance, supporting efficient reuse of multi-agent workflows for recurrent queries.

title: BT-PEC Quantum Computer Architecture and Operating System: Life-Perception Design Based on Topological Energy-Causality Theory
abstract: This paper proposes the first quantum computer architecture and operating system designed under the BT-PEC (Primitive Topological Energy-Causality) theoretical framework. Traditional quantum computing systems treat qubits as passive computing resources, while the BT-PEC architecture regards the whole quantum computer as an open quantum living system governed by topological deviation dynamics. The four BT-PEC axioms — B (Basis), T (Flux), P (Coupling), EC (Energy-Causality Closed Loop) — are mapped to hardware modules and operating system subsystems respectively. The quantum processing unit adopts a topological-logical double-layer structure, using Majorana zero modes as the physical basis and surface code for logical encoding. A coherent flux injection bus transports negative-entropy energy from the environment to quantum states. The entanglement routing network implements P coupling gate scheduling. Decoherence sensor arrays and real-time quantum error correction decoders form the EC closed loop. At the operating system level, BT-PEC/OS introduces an Ω-aware scheduler, which takes the quantum topological residual order parameter Ω_Q = T − ΔPEC as the system health indicator to drive process scheduling, resource allocation and exception handling. When Ω_Q > 0.05, tasks are executed with the highest priority; when |Ω_Q| ≤ 0.05, the system triggers automatic protection including enhanced error correction, state migration and load reduction; when Ω_Q < −0.05, the system terminates low-priority tasks and recycles quantum states. This paper presents the complete hardware architecture, kernel structure, system call interface, memory management scheme, exception handling mechanism, boot sequence and dedicated quantum programming language BPL. Comparative analysis shows that the BT-PEC architecture outperforms traditional quantum computers in self-sustainability, fault tolerance and resource efficiency. This research lays the foundation for life-state quantum computing and opens a new paradigm integrating computation and life evolution.

title: Region Aware Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks for Image Segmentation
abstract: Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) modules improve convolutional networks by modeling channel-wise dependencies, but global average pooling collapses spatial structure into a single per-channel descriptor, limiting their effectiveness for dense prediction tasks such as image segmentation. We generalize SE by replacing global pooling with spatially guided pooling, enabling region-aware channel recalibration through four modules with complementary cost profiles. BASE formalizes Tiled Squeeze-and-Excite using a regular grid; SPASE pools over SLIC superpixels for image-adaptive regions; MAPSE obtains regions from semantic maps produced by a frozen, general-purpose network; and PLEASE learns soft region assignments end-to-end through a lightweight assignment network. Each channel receives one gate per region, so attention at each pixel reflects its region membership, bridging channel and spatial attention. PLEASE also produces its soft assignments as a byproduct of the forward pass, providing structured spatial interpretability without post-hoc analysis. The modules offer complementary computational tradeoffs: some add essentially no parameters, while others add no measurable latency. Across binary segmentation on CUB, DUTS, and ECSSD, semantic segmentation on PASCAL VOC 2012 and ADE20K, and classification on mini-ImageNet, our modules outperform SE and related spatial-channel attention variants on most benchmarks, achieving the majority of best results.

title: AI-Native Product Management: A Vision
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to support product management tasks. At the same time, AI-native research and development (R&D) may increase software realization capacity. Organizations may realize software faster than they can identify, qualify, and reconsider what should be realized. This paper asks how product management should be re-envisioned under these conditions. We synthesize research on software product management, product learning, human-AI collaboration, and the Product Management and R&D boundary. We propose a vision in which AI becomes a persistent participant in product work. The vision covers sensing, exploration, decision-making, realization, and learning. We propose six principles and make the vision tangible through an operating model grounded in human professionals, AI personas, agents, skills, and a shared product context. We further argue that AI-native Product Management and AI-native R&D can form a continuous product-learning process. Finally, we identify four AI-specific research directions that require empirical investigation.

title: Hate Speech on Social Media Platforms and Its Implications for National Reconciliation from the Perspective of University Youth: A Field Study of a Sample of Students at the Faculty of Media, Al-Marj Branch, University of Benghazi
abstract: هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى معرفة مفهوم الكراهية ،وأشكاله المتداولة عبر منصات التواصل الاجتماعي، ومساهمتها في تعزيز، وتسويق خطاب الكراهية وانعكاسه على المصالحة الوطنية ،ودرجة استخدامه ، ومدى اعتماد الشباب الجامعي على منصات التواصل الاجتماعي كدليل إرشادي ـ توعوي لمواجهة خطاب الكراهية ،وتعزيز المصالحة الوطنية، و الاساليب الاتصالية الأكثر مساهمة في تسويق خطاب الكراهية ،ودرجة تأثيره على المصالحة الوطنية من وجهة نظر الشباب الجامعي ،وتوضيح أسباب أنتشار خطاب الكراهية المؤثرة على المصالحة الوطنية واليات الحد منها ،و تأثيره على منظومة القيم الاجتماعية، والثقافية للمجتمع الليبي ، و نظراً لطبيعة الدراسة ،وتحقيقاً لأهدافها اعتمد الباحث على المنهج الوصفي . حيث استخدم استمارة الاستبانة كأداة رئيسة لجمع البيانات والمعلومات وقد تكونت عينة الدراسة من (121) طالباً وطالبة موزعة على الأقسام العلمية بكلية الإعــــلام فــــرع المــــرج ، ومــــن اهـــــم النتـــائج التي توصلت إليها هـــــذه الدراسة اعتماد الشباب الجامعي بدرجة عالية جداً إلى المنصات الاجتماعية كدليل إرشادي وتوعوي لمواجهة خطاب الكراهية ، كما بينت نتائج الدراسة بــأنَ ( يوتيوب ـ سناب شات ـ فيس بوك ) مـــن أهم المنصات الاجتماعية التي تخدم المصالحة الوطنية بدرجة عالية على عكس المواقع الأخرى ( إنستغرام ـ واتس أب ـ فايبر ـ تيلجرام ـ ماسنجر ) التي جاءت بدرجة ضعيفة في خدمة المصالحة الوطنية، ووحدة الصف بين أبناء المجتمع الليبي ، كما أوضحت نتائج الدراسة تصنيف منصات التواصل الاجتماعي مـــــن وجهــــة نظـــر الشـــباب الجامعي بدرجــــة كبـــيرة كــــأداة فعالــــــــة لترويـــج ،وتسويق خطـاب الكراهية فهي تساهم ( دائماَ ) في تعزيز خطاب الكراهية ،وانعكاسه ،وتأثيره على المصالحة الوطنية في ليبيا أكَدُ أغلب الشباب الجامعي على تأثير خطاب الكراهية على القيم الاجتماعية، والدينية، والثقافية ، وقد أوصت الدراسة بضرورة وضع قيود لرقابة المنصات الاجتماعية ،وتحديد نوعية الخطاب وملاحقتهم مع وضع قوانين رادعة وقابلة للتطبيق على النشر والعرض في هذه المنصات ، وتنمية مهارة التفكير الناقد وكيفية التعامل الواعي مع محتويات منصات التواصل الاجتماعي والتميز بيت ما هو سلبي، وضار وما هو إيجابي ، ونافع ، و وضع البرامج، والأنشطة ، وتكثيف وتنسيق حملات التوعية بمخاطر التميز، وخطاب الكراهية في المنصات الاجتماعية ،وأثارها على المجتمع ، مع تنمية ثقافة التسامح، والحوار، وقبول الأخر.

title: A Technical Note on Sequential Knowledge Editing: Error Accounting, Batch Equivalence, and Zero-Cache Consolidation
abstract: Locate-then-edit methods such as MEMIT and AlphaEdit formulate factual model editing as an optimization over linear associative memories. However, sequential editing in these paradigms has consistently exhibited severe catastrophic forgetting and capability degradation over extended horizons (e.g., in recent stress-tests up to 10,000 edits). In response, recent works such as BetaEdit and EvoEdit have introduced increasingly complex geometric patches—including periodic or per-step Singular Value Decompositions (SVD)—to mitigate null-space leakage and drift. In this technical note, we demonstrate that this entire line of inquiry has been treating a symptom while overlooking the root cause. We reveal that the degradation in sequential model editing stems directly from an unjustified algebraic omission present in both MEMIT and AlphaEdit: the Historical Perfection Assumption: while preserving pre-training associations is practically sound, existing methods either omit historical edits entirely (as in sequential MEMIT) or assume they are stored with zero error (as in AlphaEdit, W K_p = V_p), silently deleting the necessary negative feedback correction on key covariance. We establish three primary results. First, we provide the full, unapproximated derivations for both batch and sequential editing without assuming zero baseline or past error. Second, we present the Fundamental Equivalence Theorem: in the unconstrained/honest objective, sequential editing is identically equivalent to all-in-one batch editing via directly expressing the sequential objective in terms of cumulative displacement and differentiating. evidence.title: A Technical Note on Sequential Knowledge Editing: Error Accounting, Batch Equivalence, and Zero-Cache Consolidation
evidence.abstract: Locate-then-edit methods such as MEMIT and AlphaEdit formulate factual model editing as an optimization over linear associative memories. However, sequential editing in these paradigms has consistently exhibited severe catastrophic forgetting and capability degradation over extended horizons (e.g., in recent stress-tests up to 10,000 edits). title: Structure-First Interpretability: Anchoring Sparse Autoencoders to the Daopology Knowledge Base
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have become the dominant tool for decomposing large language model (LLM) activations into interpretable features. Yet the field faces a fundamental crisis: there is no ground truth for what concepts a model actually uses, and a growing body of evidence shows that SAE-learned dictionaries point in substantially wrong directions, that SAE explanations suffer from descriptive collision at scale, and that SAE features fail to improve downstream tasks beyond simple baselines. This paper argues that the root cause is the absence of an external semantic reference frame—SAEs operate without an anchor. We propose a methodology that anchors SAE research to Daopology, an axiomatic system that provides 79 minimal expressive parameters for structuring knowledge across seven categories: 9 primitives, 6 Heng families, 6 Jiao families, 8 Cha families, 7 Que families, 10 Suan families, and 21 He families. We further introduce GlyphCode, a universal symbolic encoding system that renders structural entities as compositional symbol trees, and the GlyphCode Reasoner, a neuro-symbolic inference engine that operates on these trees. The proposed “structure-first” paradigm reverses the current practice: instead of asking “what does this SAE feature mean?”, we ask “which Daopology structure does this SAE feature align with?” We outline four concrete interventions—structural initialization, structural regularization, causal verification via stability criteria, and cross-model alignment via kernel isomorphism—and provide a set of falsifiable predictions. The paper positions itself as a methodology contribution, arguing that the path forward for mechanistic interpretability lies not in scaling SAEs further, but in providing them with the semantic scaffolding they currently lack.

title: Cryptography-Driven-Deterministic-Logical-Timeline-Dual-Timestamp
abstract: An AI behavior auditing system based on a deterministic logical timeline binds cryptographic states to logical moments, making every AI decision traceable, independently verifiable, and infinitely replayable. When this system is applied to scenarios involving external large-model API calls, three engineering problems arise: an API call spans multiple logical ticks while the behavior record binds only the request moment; a single mode of logical counter advancement cannot accommodate intermittent calls and continuous monitoring; and concurrent recording across multiple physical media lacks architectural guidance. This paper proposes a request-receipt dual-timestamp binding mechanism, three trigger modes (periodic, event, and hybrid), and a multi-physical-time-axis concurrent recording architecture. It provides complete data structures, algorithm flows, auditing methods, and experimental data, as prior art for free use by the industry. This paper also explicitly delineates the security boundaries and trust assumptions of each mechanism, and provides engineering implementation schemes for authentication tag construction, clock trust models, and cross-axis causality proofs.

title: Hypergraph-Augmented Reconstruction and Adaptive Metric Aggregation Network for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Image Classification
abstract: Few-shot fine-grained image classification aims to recognize unseen fine-grained categories from very few labeled examples. The task is difficult because visually similar classes may differ only in subtle details, while images from the same class can vary considerably. Useful evidence is therefore often localized. Reconstruction-based metric methods reduce local misalignment by reconstructing query features from class-wise support features, but a small support set may still provide an incomplete reconstruction basis. In addition, spatial reconstruction errors are usually combined with fixed or nearly uniform weights, and intermediate features receive no direct reconstruction-oriented supervision. We develop HARA, a Hypergraph-Augmented Reconstruction and Adaptive Metric Aggregation Network, to address these limitations. HARA forms learnable soft hyperedges over local support features and uses the resulting aggregated features to enrich the class-wise reconstruction basis. It then combines class-conditional reconstruction with query self-reconstruction to obtain position-wise joint errors, which are aggregated using query-dependent weights. A training-only auxiliary branch applies reconstruction-based supervision to intermediate backbone features. For 5-way evaluation, HARA obtains 84.09%/93.48% on CUB-200-2011, 76.91%/88.69% on Stanford Dogs and 88.53%/95.87% on Stanford Cars under the 1-shot/5-shot settings, respectively. Ablation and diagnostic analyses further characterize the contributions and behavior of the proposed framework. Overall, HARA provides an effective extension to reconstruction-based few-shot fine-grained classification.

title: On the Theoretical Limits of Learning Unconstrained Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) accelerate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by learning the energies and forces that govern atomic motion. Recent work has shown that relaxing physical inductive biases can improve computational efficiency and predictive accuracy, raising the question of whether energy-and-force matching alone is sufficient to ensure accurate sampling. We show that, for unconstrained hypothesis classes, the relationship between prediction error and sampling accuracy is exponentially ill-conditioned in dimension. In particular, prediction errors that decay exponentially with dimension can coexist with nearly maximal total variation distance between the learned and target distributions. We identify two failure mechanisms. The first is kinetic trapping, where relaxation to an accurate learned equilibrium requires exponentially long times, even when simulations are initialized from training configurations at which energies and forces are matched exactly. The second is equilibrium mismatch, where the learned stationary distribution itself remains far from the target. Under explicit assumptions, we show that equilibrium mismatch can persist even in local, symmetry-preserving models, where small per-atom errors coexist with a distributional discrepancy that approaches its maximum as system size increases. Finally, we establish global energy-control conditions that guarantee equilibrium accuracy and identify additional conditions required for rapid relaxation.

title: Dissecting the Carbon-SLO Tension in Geo-Distributed LLM Serving
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) inference is driving a growing share of datacenter carbon emissions. Although carbon-aware scheduling can reduce these emissions in geo-distributed datacenters by exploiting the spatiotemporal variations in grid carbon intensity, the latency-sensitive nature of LLM serving constrains this design space. While prior studies investigate the carbon savings achievable through spatial scheduling, they oversimplify the dynamics of modern inference engines, such as queueing and continuous batching, which strongly shape inference latency. We address this issue by designing and evaluating a latency-centric, geo-distributed inference simulator, calibrated with hardware-grounded latency and power measurements, that reproduces these dynamics and enables the study of carbon savings under strict service-level objectives (SLOs). We then formulate a series of SLO- and carbon-aware schedulers of increasing sophistication, from per-request heuristics to batch-level optimization: (i) a greedy heuristic, (ii) an integer linear programming (ILP)-based scheduler jointly assigning batches of requests, (iii) an iterative ILP-based solution projecting its own assignments back into the load estimates to capture load coupling, and (iv) a facility mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) scheduler pricing the energy of batched requests collectively rather than in isolation. Across three LLMs under MLPerf SLOs and varying system loads, the MILP-based option offers the best carbon-SLO balance, reducing carbon emissions by up to 60% relative to the round-robin policy, with an average SLO violation of 3%. Our characterization further shows that savings grow with the spread of carbon intensity across datacenters and shrink as system load increases, while SLO attainment depends on how frequently schedulers receive datacenters' load updates.

title: DS and AMDS Symbol-Pair Codes from Three Families of Simple Root Cyclic Codes
abstract: Symbol-pair distances of simple-root cyclic codes are important for evaluating error correction performance under overlapping pair read channels. In this paper, we construct three families of simple-root cyclic codes over finite fields of odd characteristic via generator polynomials. For length \(2q+2\), the minimum symbol-pair distance is \(10\) for every odd prime power \(q\ge 7\), established by excluding invalid support configurations. For length \(4q-4\), when \(q\equiv 3\pmod 4\) and finite field constraints hold, it is \(9\) or \(10\). For length \(2(q-1)\), reciprocal-polynomial analysis shows it is \(11\) or \(12\). All obtained codes are MDS or AMDS symbol-pair codes.

title: Data, programs and VIPR certificates for “The largest minimum distance of ternary LCD codes of dimensions four and five”
abstract: Data set (version 1.0.2) of the paper “The largest minimum distance of ternary LCD codes of dimensions four and five” by K. Promjiraprawat, W. Wongseree and D. Setsirichok. LCD_package_v1.0.2.zip holds the generator matrices of all codes, the programs, the integer-programming models, the solver logs, the result files and the LaTeX source of the paper; its README.md maps each statement of the paper to the files and the command that check it, and python3 src/verify_all.py re-checks the codes and the proofs’ counts and regenerates the paper’s tables. The other 35 files hold the VIPR certificates of infeasibility for the 73 integer programs of Section 6.4, produced by SCIP 10.1.0 with SoPlex 8.1.0 in exact mode and checked by viprchk: the zip archives LCD_vipr_certificates_v1.0.1_01.zip to _07.zip hold the 66 certificates of at most 200 MB, and the 7 larger ones are cut into pieces NAME.vipr.xz.partNN of 200,000,000 bytes. LCD_vipr_certificates_v1.0.1_contents.txt lists which certificate is in which file, with the SHA-256 and MD5 of every file. To use the certificates, download the files into one directory DIR, unpack the package and run python3 src/join_certificates.py DIR, which joins the pieces and checks every certificate against the SHA-256 recorded in results.jsonl.

title: Two-Stage Measurement of Update Adherence in Language Model Memory Agents: benchmark, event records, and scoring scripts
abstract: Benchmark scenarios, event records, frozen memory engine, and scoring scripts for the paper "Two-Stage Measurement of Update Adherence in Language Model Memory Agents". Update Adherence (UA) measures whether a revised requirement, and not the statement it replaced, governs the answer of a language model agent with external memory. It is scored at two stages with deterministic rules and no language-model judge, in the assembled context that the memory system hands to the answering model and in the generated answer. Every number in the paper can be recomputed from the files in this archive with python analysis/make_tables.py. Code is under the MIT License. Scenario data, result data, and figure data are under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA).

title: HEAIN-SD-1.0: การสรางคำบรรยายและการพากยเสยงภาษาไทยทกำกบดวยนโยบายบนโหนด Hybrid Edge AI
abstract: ระบบพากย์เสียงอัตโนมัติในปัจจุบันสร้างเสียงที่ฟังเข้าใจได้แล้ว แต่งานคำบรรยายและงานพากย์ระดับมืออาชีพยังติดปัญหาสามข้อที่ไม่ค่อยได้รับการแก้พร้อมกัน ข้อแรก อารมณ์ในการส่งเสียงต้องมีผู้ที่อ่านภาพเป็นผู้กำกับ ข้อสอง เนื้อหาที่มีคำหยาบหรือต้อง censor ต้องเป็นไปตามกฎที่ต่างกันตามประเทศและแพลตฟอร์มปลายทาง และข้อสาม การบันทึกเสียงที่ทำให้ระบบเก่งขึ้นเป็นข้อมูลส่วนบุคคลของเจ้าของเสียงที่ระบุตัวตนได้ บทความนี้เสนอ HEAIN-SD-1.0 ซึ่งเป็นโปรไฟล์ระดับแอปพลิเคชัน (Application Profile) ที่กำหนดว่าโมดูลสร้างคำบรรยายและพากย์เสียงที่เน้นภาษาไทยทำงานอย่างไรในฐานะ Layer 3 (Application AI) บน HEAIN Core Protocol และสถาปัตยกรรม Hybrid Edge AI Node บทความนำเสนอผลงานสี่ข้อ ข้อแรก บันไดความอัตโนมัติที่กำกับด้วยนโยบาย (L0–L3) ซึ่งระบบเรียนรู้ได้ทุกอย่างเกี่ยวกับการส่งเสียง แต่ไม่เรียนรู้ว่าอะไรอนุญาตให้พูด เพราะนโยบายเนื้อหาเป็นคลังที่มีเจ้าของแยกต่างหาก เลือกตามปลายทาง และ fail-closed ข้อสอง การแยกเสียงพากย์เป็นสี่ส่วน โดยเนื้อเสียงมาจากการแสดงต้นฉบับ สำเนียงมาจากมาตรฐานของทีมพากย์มืออาชีพในประเทศเป้าหมาย และอารมณ์กับจังหวะมาจากคำกำกับของโปรดิวเซอร์ ซึ่งทำได้ด้วยการสังเคราะห์เสียงที่ใช้ตัวอย่างซึ่งค้นมาเป็นพรอมต์จากคลังการส่งเสียงมืออาชีพที่ได้รับความยินยอม ข้อสาม โปรไฟล์โปรโตคอลที่มีแบบจำลอง session การแบ่งโซน CORE/EDGE และรายการขาขึ้นที่อนุญาต ซึ่งเก็บสื่อไว้ที่โหนดประมวลผล และส่งขึ้นโหนดควบคุมเฉพาะระเบียนข้อมูล คะแนน และ embedding ขนาดเล็ก ข้อสี่ แผนการประเมินผลที่กำหนดเกณฑ์ผ่านไว้ก่อนการทดลองใดๆ บทความนี้ไม่มีผลการทดลอง โปรไฟล์เป็นแบบที่ยังไม่ได้พัฒนาจริง และทุกปริมาณที่ระบุว่าเป็นค่าประมาณคือค่าที่ใช้วางแผน คำสำคัญ: Automatic Dubbing, Subtitling, ภาษาไทย, Voice Cloning, ภาษามีวรรณยุกต์, Human-in-the-Loop, นโยบายเนื้อหา, Edge Computing, การจัดการความยินยอม, ข้อกำหนดโปรโตคอล

title: AUŠRA: The Architectural Impact of Intuition, Instinct, and Quarantine on Decision Speed, Threat Detection, Authorization, and Survival A Synthetic Causal Exploration of the Integrated AUŠRA–EGIDA–LASO-Σ–KASK-Q–BITE Architecture
abstract: AUŠRA: Scientific Significance and Architectural Contribution Authors: Egidijus Kasiulevičius, Ąžuolas Kasiulevičius, Saulė Kasiulevičiūtė, Aušra KasiulevičienėDate: 10 October 2026 Summary AUŠRA is an integrated autonomous decision-making architecture designed to coordinate rapid response, information retrieval, conditional authorization, threat detection, quarantine, and adaptive feedback. The research investigates how adding INSTINCT, INTUITION, and QUARANTINE may change the behavior of the complete AUŠRA architecture, including EGIDA, LASO-Σ, KASK-Q, and BITE. The central principle is that improving an autonomous system does not necessarily mean increasing every performance metric simultaneously. Faster decisions may introduce risks; additional interpretation may improve threat detection while increasing decision time; and quarantine may reduce false actions while also suppressing relevant signals if its rules are too restrictive. AUŠRA therefore treats these mechanisms as complementary components whose individual effects and interactions must be evaluated together. Key significance to science 1. A system-level approach to autonomous decision-making The research emphasizes that decision speed, accuracy, authorization, and survival are interconnected properties of an architecture. A component's value cannot be established solely by measuring its isolated performance. 2. The coordination of fast response and controlled authorization INSTINCT represents a fast protective-response pathway, while LASO-Σ preserves conditional authorization. The architectural question is how to reduce dangerous delays without granting unrestricted authority to emergency actions. 3. The trade-off between threat detection and information quarantine INTUITION and QUARANTINE illustrate different potential trade-offs. Additional interpretation may improve detection at the cost of processing time, while excessive isolation may reduce false actions but increase missed threats. These effects require causal testing rather than assumptions about which component is beneficial. 4. A method for investigating component interactions The research proposes evaluating individual contributions, interactions, and full-system outcomes through matched scenarios, experimental ablations, independent repetitions, and uncertainty estimates. Modules are isolated for testing, not automatically removed from the architecture. 5. A measurable framework for safety-aware optimization The proposed evaluation combines decision steps, critical-threat detection, false-action rates, authorization violations, and safe outcomes before a deadline. This avoids declaring success based on speed alone. Preliminary results and scientific boundaries In the previously reported synthetic M6.9 model, the integrated AUŠRA configuration showed: Decision steps: 99.9 to 94.9. Critical-threat detection: 90.49% to 91.44%. False-action rate: 10.82% to 8.78%. Safe outcomes before the deadline: 42.07% to 50.88%. These are descriptive results from a synthetic exploratory model, not independently validated measurements of a deployed AUŠRA implementation. Statistical significance and real-world performance advantages have not yet been established. The current research status is M6.9 — PARTIAL PASS. Conclusion The principal scientific contribution is a testable architectural framework for investigating how rapid protective response, interpretation, information isolation, conditional authorization, structural information addressing, and adaptive feedback can be coordinated within one autonomous system. The research does not assume that every module improves every metric. Instead, it investigates the conditions under which each component contributes to the overall balance between speed, decision quality, authorization, and safety. The next scientific step is independent, reproducible causal evaluation of the integrated architecture. title: "DGRP-miniF2F-PISA-ControlBench"
abstract: "Beyond retrieving established facts, formal theorem proving often requires formulating auxiliary lemmas and coordinating their logical dependencies. We represent proof dependencies as an executable directed acyclic graph (DAG) and propose DGRP (DAG-Guided Recursive Prover). Within this graph, a language model generates auxiliary lemmas for recursive decomposition or synthesizes direct formal proof scripts. To reuse decomposition patterns across theorems, DGRP maintains a persistent decomposition memory of local decomposition records checked in their source theory contexts and retrieves them to guide auxiliary lemma generation for subsequent theorems. We evaluate DGRP on miniF2F, a continuous mathematics subset extracted via PISA, and our designed ControlBench. On miniF2F with Gemini 3.1 Pro, combining DAG structuring with recursive refinement raises the pass@3 verification rate from 38.1\\% for a direct formal prover to 69.7\\% for DGRP without decomposition memory. Across evaluated settings, decomposition memory provides an additional improvement of up to 4.7 percentage points. These results provide empirical evidence that explicitly organizing proof dependencies and reusing decomposition patterns can improve automated formal reasoning."

title: BrainAid: Efficient Brain Tumor Detection Using Lightweight CNNs and Explainable AI for Resource-Constrained Environments
abstract: A brain tumor is an unusual growth of cells in the brain that can be cancerous or not, affecting normal brain function and causing serious risk to health. Existing solutions for brain tumor classification, such as expert manual evaluations of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, are generally inconsistent as different professionals have different criteria and can be resource-intensive, leading to delayed diagnoses. Additionally, while deep learning models have demonstrated potential, they typically require significant computational resources, motivating the need for more efficient and accessible diagnostic tools that can be deployed in real-time healthcare settings. To address these limitations, this study presents BrainAid, which makes efficient use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) for effective classification of four-class classification of glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no-tumor MRI scans, outperforming all the standard models such as VGG16, Inception-V3, ResNet-50 and so, while integrating Explainable AI (XAI) to improve interpretability. The BrainAid is trained to classify tumors with a high precision of 98%, achieving an F1 score of 98% and an accuracy of 98% using publicly available dataset. The model is deployed on a Raspberry Pi, demonstrating efficiency in low-resource environments. This system shows the feasibility of real-time, edge-based tumor classification, providing quick diagnostic support for medical professionals and enhancing patient care in resource-limited healthcare facilities and underserved areas.

title: Explore This! Beat and Downbeat Tracking From a Learned Tatum Grid
abstract: State-of-the-art beat tracking is based on neural networks that model beats and downbeats as individual events, often followed by a separate Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) enforcing musical consistency. We propose a novel architecture that combines deep learning with differentiable theory-based modules: Specifically, we design a system that first predicts a tatum grid, then groups tatum events to beats and downbeats, explicitly modelling multiple options for the current tempo and time signature in a bar-pointer-like fashion. Our approach improves continuity metrics compared to existing DBN-free systems and is more versatile than the de-facto standard DBN, but still falls behind the best DBN-based methods on average. Given the many design choices and hyperparameters involved, we assume we have not yet explored the full potential of this idea and publish our code and invite others to explore this further.

title: Enhancing Knowledge Management in Green Building Engineering: A Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Approach to Support Project Assessment
abstract: Abstract Green building assessment relies heavily on manual queries of complex engineering regulations, making the introduction of knowledge management theories crucial for improving assessment efficiency. However, the inherent characteristics of engineering regulations—dense terminology, complex clause dependencies, and frequent revisions—limit the effectiveness of traditional knowledge engineering. This study aims to explore the utilization of advanced information technologies to achieve reliable knowledge management for supporting engineering decision-making. From the perspective of acquisition, organization, retrieval, and presentation (AORP), a domain knowledge management framework is designed by integrating network analysis, information retrieval, and large language models (LLMs) with traditional knowledge management theories. A dual-structure knowledge network is proposed as the underlying carrier to characterize explicit rules and semantic dependencies, enabling lightweight knowledge organization. Furthermore, a hybrid retrieval algorithm capable of identifying and adaptively weighting domain terms was developed and embedded into a retrieval-augmented generation workflow. Facilitated by LLMs, the proposed framework supports more efficient, traceable, and scalable building assessment. This study covers regulations containing 225,604 words and validates the effectiveness of the proposed method using 132 practical test cases. The results showed that the proposed method achieves a recall rate of 0.959, effectively reduces generation hallucinations, and substantially improves the accuracy and reliability of knowledge presentation. More importantly, the experiments indicated that the performance gap among LLMs with different parameter scales narrowed after introducing domain knowledge, confirming that an effective knowledge management architecture in vertical domains has the potential to reduce dependence on large-parameter LLMs and provide a feasible pathway for low-cost deployment of intelligent applications in the industry.

This study covers regulations containing 225,604 words and validates the effectiveness of the proposed method using 132 practical test cases. The results showed that the proposed method achieves a recall rate of 0.959, effectively reduces generation hallucinations, and substantially improves the accuracy and reliability of knowledge presentation. More importantly, the experiments indicated that the performance gap among LLMs with different parameter scales narrowed after introducing domain knowledge, confirming that an effective knowledge management architecture in vertical domains has the potential to reduce dependence on large-parameter LLMs and provide a feasible pathway for low-cost deployment of intelligent applications in the industry.
